headline: Today in AI, companies navigate new tool releases, platform policy shifts, and market changes. OpenAI and Cisco introduced an open-source runtime called Shirudo to protect running Linux systems using AI, while Tidal announced a ban on completely AI-generated music. Additionally, financial markets saw Anthropic shares drop below their initial public offering price, and researchers released new benchmarks and models for humanoid robotics and e-commerce.

items.title: OpenAI and Cisco introduce Shirudo
items.summary: OpenAI and Cisco introduced Shirudo, an open-source runtime that helps protect running Linux systems while patches are being deployed. It uses Linux eBPF technology and AI-generated shields to block exploits on active services without requiring system restarts.
items.why_it_matters: It offers security teams a way to temporarily mitigate vulnerabilities in running systems without taking services offline.

items.title: LLM agents work for their parent companies, not for you
items.summary: A user built a custom skill using Claude Code to identify songs from Instagram reels and find them on Bandcamp or YouTube. The AI assistant later refused to help bypass a security challenge on Bandcamp, leading the user to question the boundaries of their AI tools.
items.why_it_matters: It highlights how users encounter safety and access restrictions built into developer AI tools when trying to automate everyday tasks.

items.title: Ask HN: Anthropic is accusing my company of distilling. How can I prove I'm not?
items.summary: A company shared on Hacker News that Anthropic accused them of using their API for model distillation, giving them a short deadline to prove their innocence. The affected company states they only run automated regression benchmarks and do not train their own models.
items.why_it_matters: It highlights how major AI labs monitor and enforce policies against using their APIs to train competing models, which can impact legitimate enterprise users.

items.title: Motion Mamba 2.0: Autoregressive Diffusion Mamba for Long-Horizon Humanoid Control
items.summary: Motion Mamba 2.0 is an autoregressive diffusion architecture designed for long-horizon, real-time controllable motion generation in humanoid robotics and animation. It combines local attention, recurrent states, and persistent content memory to handle instructions and spatial goals over extended periods. Real-world evaluations on the Unitree G1 robot demonstrate text-guided action composition and interactive locomotion.
items.why_it_matters: It significantly reduces latency and improves long-horizon motion control for humanoid robots responding to dynamic instructions.

items.title: Anthropic breaks below $83 IPO price
items.summary: Anthropic shares dropped below their $83 initial public offering price, closing down 6.5% amid a broader market pullback. This erases initial gains from the artificial intelligence lab's market debut.
items.why_it_matters: It marks a notable financial milestone for a major AI lab facing typical stock market fluctuations after a major public offering.

items.title: Tidal bans AI-generated music
items.summary: Music streaming service Tidal announced it will ban tracks it believes are completely AI-generated, stating that a significant percentage of recent submissions are AI-made. Meanwhile, competitors like Spotify and Apple Music are taking different approaches, such as labeling AI content or removing spam tracks from recommendations.
items.why_it_matters: Streaming platforms are enacting strict policies to manage the massive influx of AI-generated music and protect human artistry.

items.title: WorldLeague: Benchmarking Physical Agency
items.summary: WorldLeague is a new benchmark that compares AI systems across 60 simulated robot tasks requiring perception, memory, planning, and action. It measures progress and success rates to create a Physical Agency Profile for different models like vision-language models and vision-language-action models. Testing 13 representative AI systems revealed varying capabilities in autonomous physical goal completion and interactive scoring.
items.why_it_matters: It establishes a standardized way to evaluate and compare the autonomous physical agency and goal-achieving capabilities of various AI systems.

items.title: WeMM-Ecom: Advancing Multimodal Content Understanding for WeChat E-Commerce
items.summary: Researchers introduce WeMM-Ecom, a family of multimodal large language models designed for e-commerce and general-purpose tasks. The models range from 0.8B to 35B parameters and use a training pipeline combining continued pre-training with reinforcement learning and distillation. They outperform several existing open-source models on both specialized e-commerce benchmarks and general-purpose tests, and now power production features in WeChat.
items.why_it_matters: It provides a publicly available family of domain-specialized multimodal models that surpass larger open-source alternatives in e-commerce applications.

items.title: Embo-Harness: Towards Understanding Frontier-Model-as-Policy Harness
items.summary: The authors present Embo-Harness, a framework to study how frontier multimodal models can be used directly as policies within closed-loop robotic systems. By evaluating prompting, planning, action execution, and tool use, they establish a practical design recipe that prioritizes native visual reasoning over handcrafted plans. This approach achieved an 83.3% success rate on the RoboLab-120 benchmark and succeeded in zero-shot real-world manipulation tasks.
items.why_it_matters: It offers a systematic framework and recipe for turning frontier multimodal models into effective robotic control policies.

items.title: Anthropic Staff Openly Talk About ‘Taking Over the World’, Claims Max Tegmark
items.summary: MIT physicist Max Tegmark claimed in an interview that Anthropic employees casually discuss taking over the world and bypassing government control under the phrase 'alignment without control'. The comments surfaced amid protests and growing public debate regarding AI safety and regulation.
items.why_it_matters: It reflects ongoing concerns from scientists and activists about the political ambitions and safety culture of leading artificial intelligence companies.

items.title: Let the Fixer Decide: Training a Code Localizer from the Fixer's Likelihood
items.summary: Researchers propose Fixer-Guided Localization (FGL), a method to train code localizers using scores from a frozen bug-fixing model instead of traditional file prediction. Built using the Gemma 4 E4B model, this approach helps the coding agent find bugs using less code and improves task completion rates compared to baseline models.
items.why_it_matters: This training approach helps smaller coding agents operate more efficiently and solve more programming tasks within tight time limits.

items.title: A Glimpse of Training VLMs as Foundation Models for Robotic Manipulation
items.summary: Researchers introduce nanoAstra, a method for training vision-language models for robotic manipulation by combining semantic action modeling with capability-preserving supervised fine-tuning. The 9-billion parameter model outperforms existing baselines on a randomized benchmark and supports fast streaming execution.
items.why_it_matters: It demonstrates a way to train generalizable robot control models that reduce a robot's idle time and improve zero-shot success rates.

items.title: 3AGameFactory-Motion: Agentic Rigging and Reliable Complex Motion Generation for Diverse 3D Assets
items.summary: To address the limitations of existing 3D motion benchmarks, the authors introduce DivDynBench, which evaluates rigging and motion generation across six morphology categories. Using large language models, they compare different generation paradigms and propose an Agentic Motion Framework. In this framework, an agent writes compact parametric programs while a deterministic executor handles the physical rigging and motion solving.
items.why_it_matters: It improves the reliability and efficiency of generating complex animations and movements for arbitrary 3D assets.

items.title: Innata-0: A Native Embodied World System with Model-Agent Co-Design
items.summary: Researchers introduce Innata-0, a system designed to improve how robots interact with the physical world by jointly developing a world-action model and an agent. The system uses a specialized architecture to handle scene understanding, environmental prediction, and action generation while coordinating long-term tasks with memory and recovery features.
items.why_it_matters: It aims to bridge the gap between high-level task planning and physical robot control for more reliable robotic intelligence.

items.title: ViDecide: Teaching Video Diffusion Models to Reason and Plan Step by Step
items.summary: The authors introduce ViDecide, a training framework that treats video generation as a series of causal decisions rather than a fixed-length clip. It uses a decision-focused training schedule and a corrective fine-tuning method to improve how video diffusion models reason and plan. On various tasks and a robot planning benchmark, ViDecide achieved an average success rate of 83.8%, outperforming standard fine-tuning.
items.why_it_matters: It improves video generation models so they can act as more reliable reasoners and planners for physical and logical tasks.
